tagline: From yuenyeung to pour-over: how coffee became Hong Kong's social glue.
why: Coffee is the easiest small talk there is: almost everyone drinks it and has a favourite spot. Hong Kong has gone from instant coffee and cha chaan teng milk coffee to one of Asia's best specialty coffee scenes. Knowing the drinks, the brewing methods and a few local names lets you talk cafés, origins and trends with anyone.

essentials.title: Arabica vs robusta
essentials.body: Arabica beans are smoother and more aromatic, used in specialty coffee. Robusta is stronger, more bitter and has more caffeine.

essentials.title: Origins taste different
essentials.body: Ethiopian beans are often fruity and floral, Colombian balanced, Brazilian nutty and chocolatey, Indonesian earthy.

essentials.title: Roast level
essentials.body: Light roasts keep fruity origin flavours; dark roasts taste roasty and bitter. Specialty cafés favour light to medium.

essentials.title: Espresso drinks
essentials.body: Espresso is the base. Add hot water for an Americano, steamed milk for a latte or flat white, foam for a cappuccino.

essentials.title: Filter coffee
essentials.body: Pour-over (like V60), French press, AeroPress and cold brew bring out different flavours. Pour-over is the specialty café ritual.

essentials.title: Third wave
essentials.body: The 'third wave' treats coffee like wine: single origins, light roasts, careful brewing. First wave was instant; second was Starbucks.

Arabica prices soar on bad harvests.
Coffee prices hit records; Luckin opens in Hong Kong.

now.headline: Coffee is expensive
now.detail: Bad harvests in Brazil and Vietnam pushed bean prices to record highs, raising café prices.

now.headline: Chinese chains go global
now.detail: Luckin and other Chinese chains sell cheap, app-ordered coffee and are expanding abroad.

now.headline: Specialty everywhere
now.detail: Light roasts, pour-overs and fancy origins are mainstream in Asian cities.

now.headline: Climate risk
now.detail: Coffee farms face drought and heat; some scientists worry arabica land will shrink.

local.headline: Cha chaan teng coffee
local.detail: Hong Kong-style coffee is strong and served with evaporated milk. Ask for 'yuenyeung' if you want both coffee and tea.

local.headline: Specialty hotspots
local.detail: Sheung Wan, Sai Ying Pun, Tai Hang and Sham Shui Po are full of independent cafés.

local.headline: Cheap vs specialty
local.detail: Luckin's low prices vs HK$50+ specialty lattes is a current debate.

local.headline: Barista champions
local.detail: Hong Kong baristas regularly place well at international competitions.

debates.question: Starbucks or independent?
debates.sides: Convenience and consistency vs quality and character.

debates.question: Light or dark roast?
debates.sides: Bright fruity flavours vs classic bold coffee.

debates.question: Is HK$50 for a latte reasonable?
debates.sides: Rent and wages vs daily affordability.

debates.question: Milk or black?
debates.sides: Purists say black shows the bean; most people prefer milk.
